etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English monstrous, from Old French monstrueuse, monstrüos, from Latin mōnstrōsus. Compare monstruous.

quote.citation: c. 1596–1599 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Second Part of Henry the Fourth, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene iii]:
quote.text: So bad a death argues a monstrous life.

quote.citation: c. 1603–1604 (date written), William Shakespeare, The Tragœdy of Othello, the Moore of Venice. […] (First Quarto), London:  […]  N[icholas] O[kes] for Thomas Walkley, […], published 1622, →OCLC, [Act II, scene i], page 21:
quote.text: The chiding billovv ſeemes to pelt the cloudes, / The vvinde ſhak'd ſurge, vvith high and monſtrous mayne, / Seemes to caſt vvater, on the burning Beare,  […]

quote.citation: 1901 December 20, “The Ringing of Plants”, in The Agricultural Journal and Mining Record‎[1], volume 4, number 21, page 663:
quote.text: Possibly monster pumpkins may become still more monstrous by the shoots being ringed, and so may other vegetables and fruits where quality is of less importance than mere size.

quote.citation: 1689 (indicated as 1690), [John Locke], chapter 3, in An Essay Concerning Humane Understanding. […], London:  […]  Eliz[abeth] Holt, for Thomas Basset, […], →OCLC:
1650, Jeremy Taylor, The rule and exercises of holy living:
quote.text: He, therefore, that refuses to do good to them whom he is bound to love  […]  is unnatural and monstrous in his affections.

definitions.definition: Of, or relating to a mythical monster; full of monsters.

quote.citation: 1637, John Milton, “Lycidas”, in Poems of Mr. John Milton, […], London:  […]  Ruth Raworth for Humphrey Mosely, […], published 1646, →OCLC:
quote.text: Where thou, perhaps, under the whelming tide / Visitest the bottom of the monstrous world.

quote.citation: 1886 October – 1887 January, H[enry] Rider Haggard, She: A History of Adventure, London: Longmans, Green, and Co., published 1887, →OCLC:
quote.text: The whole story was monstrous, and only worthy of the superstitious days in which it was written.
